business_problem: Microsoft's Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs organization needed to monitor and interpret fast-changing regulations at high quality and speed, but manual legal review took hours per regulation and made it difficult to scale compliance analysis consistently across the department.
solution_summary: Microsoft's CELA organization worked with EY Law and technology teams to build a generative AI workflow for regulatory compliance. After reviewing more than 250 potential use cases, the teams ran an intensive two-day workshop on data strategy, privacy, confidentiality and legal work product, then designed a regulatory-space proof of concept integrated with the EY Global Tax Platform. The solution uses Microsoft Azure Open AI and Microsoft Semantic Kernel to ingest new regulations, summarize them, identify next steps and generate formatted emails and implementation guidance artifacts for CELA stakeholders. Beyond chat, the workflow captures scope, compliance dates, trust domains, citations, defined terms and fields from regulatory text. Rapid iteration with lawyers and product teams turned the POC into a pilot implementation in the legal department and yielded reusable skillsets for document understanding, automated document generation, predictive action and position tracking.

The integrated solution then populates implementation-guidance artifacts and email outputs for CELA stakeholders, and lawyers refine the workflow through pilot feedback and additional use-case expansion.
business_outcome: Microsoft shortened regulatory-compliance analysis from hours to minutes, created a pilotable GenAI workflow for legal work and established reusable compliance skillsets that can accelerate additional Azure-based AI deployments across CELA.
